storylines.storyline_label: Unsloth Dynamic GGUF squeezes Z.ai's 744B open-weight GLM-5.2 onto a single workstation (1.51TB checkpoint cut to ~217-239GB)
storylines.last_state_change_kind: New artifact shipped (June 23): Unsloth published Dynamic GGUF quantizations of Z.ai's newly open-weighted GLM-5.2 (744B mixture-of-experts, ~40B active, 1M-token context). Selective-precision scheme upcasts accuracy-sensitive layers to 8/16-bit and pushes the rest to 1-2 bit, shrinking the 1.51TB checkpoint to ~239GB (2-bit UD-IQ2_M, 84% reduction) and ~217GB (1-bit, ~86%), runnable on a high-memory single-node box; paired with Unsloth Studio local execution; compression/quality claims are Unsloth's own, not independently reproduced. NOTE for today: a fresh continuation needs a NEW concrete artifact/number (e.g. an independent reproduction publishing accuracy retention, a new quant build/tag, a different model getting the same treatment, or a named third party running it). A restatement of the same June 23 GGUF builds with no new fact must be DROPPED as hold-steady under ADR-002 Rule 2.

storylines.storyline_label: Agentic-AI security moves from hypothetical to documented: OWASP State of Agentic AI Security & Governance v2.01 ties risks to real CVEs + StakeBench finds no injection-robust configuration
storylines.last_state_change_kind: New artifacts (June 23): OWASP's State of Agentic AI Security and Governance v2.01 tracks 53 agentic projects, ties nearly every risk category to concrete CVEs/advisories/breach reports, counts 28 coding agents, ranks most-advisory repos (n8n 57, Claude Code 22, AutoGPT 15, Dify 13, Roo-Code 11), flags 7 projects shipping daily-or-faster, and maps prompt injection to 6 of its 10 Top-10 categories. StakeBench (NTU, ST Engineering, IBM Research, UIUC) ran 3,168 trials: indirect-injection success 41.67-68.16%, direct >79% across every config, none robust; model-swap shifted indirect success by up to 26.49pp. Microsoft's prior Semantic Kernel RCE disclosure anchors the vendor side. NOTE for today: a fresh continuation needs a NEW state-change (a new report version, a new named benchmark/result, a new CVE/advisory or breach, or a procurement/standards body citing a numeric bar). Re-citing the same v2.01 + StakeBench figures must be DROPPED under ADR-002 Rule 2.

storylines.storyline_label: Coding-agent harnesses converge on least-privilege-by-default execution (OpenClaw 2026.6.x patches, NVIDIA NemoClaw, Nous Hermes Agent MCP credential filtering)
storylines.last_state_change_kind: New artifacts / actor positions (June 23): OpenClaw's June 2026.6.x releases patched vCard + location-pin injection, tightened Docker sandbox boundaries, added Browser CDP endpoint validation, pinned SSH tunnel checks to loopback, and began rejecting unsafe chat/tool/package/response lengths (plus first-class OpenRouter onboarding). NVIDIA's NemoClaw (open reference stack for always-on agents inside OpenShell sandboxes) prioritizes sandbox hardening, credential handling, and stricter network-policy defaults. Nous Research's Hermes Agent adds MCP credential filtering (only approved env vars to subprocesses), credential redaction, SSRF protection, and a Tirith pre-execution scan. NOTE for today: a fresh continuation needs a NEW named release/tag or feature that makes gating a shipped default (e.g. a tagged OpenClaw/NemoClaw/Hermes build whose default profile is default-deny on a clean install), not a restatement of the same hardening throughline, which must be DROPPED under ADR-002 Rule 2.

A still-pending/unchanged status must remain DROPPED under ADR-002 Rule 2 — do not re-run the scheduled-but-unconfirmed vote.

storylines.storyline_label: AWS New York Summit agent stack: AWS Context (governed agentic-search knowledge graph) + AWS Continuum (AI-native sandbox-validated code-vulnerability service) + Bedrock AgentCore Guardrails/optimization analytics
storylines.last_state_change_kind: New artifacts shipped (June 17 summit, coverage into June 20-21): AWS Context (auto-built governed knowledge graph exposed as a runtime, access-controlled agentic-search layer), AWS Continuum (model-agnostic vuln-management service running discover/prioritize/sandbox-validate-by-building-a-working-exploit/remediate, gated preview, leans on frontier models incl. Claude Mythos), and Bedrock AgentCore Guardrails (prompt-injection/harmful-content/sensitive-data screening) plus optimization analytics. NOTE for today: 3+ days old and not re-run since June 21 — only eligible for a continuation bullet if a NEW concrete state-change lands (GA/pricing, a named pilot/customer, a benchmark, or a competitor matching Continuum's sandbox proof-of-exploit). Otherwise DROP under ADR-002 Rule 2.

storylines.storyline_label: OpenAI beneficial-trait reinforcement learning: small dose of trait-targeted RL generalizes broadly and hardens models against jailbreaks + harmful fine-tuning
storylines.last_state_change_kind: New research artifact (June 19, alignment.openai.com + PDF): 'Reinforcement Learning Towards Broadly and Persistently Beneficial Models' reports improvement on 44/53 independent benchmarks, cross-domain generalization, 'selective persistence' under adversarial prompts, and reduced trait erosion under harmful fine-tuning; framed as distinct from Anthropic's explicit constitution; self-reported, awaiting reproduction. NOTE for today: 3+ days old and not re-run since June 21 — a fresh continuation needs a NEW state-change (independent reproduction, a critique/rebuttal, or a frontier lab shipping a beneficial-trait/persona-RL stage in a production model card). A restatement of the same June 19 paper must be DROPPED under ADR-002 Rule 2.

storylines.storyline_label: OpenAI LifeSciBench + GPT-Rosalind: 750-task expert-rubric life-science research benchmark exposing the artifact-vs-text gap
storylines.last_state_change_kind: New evaluation artifact (released June 17, secondary coverage into June 20-21): LifeSciBench built with 173 PhD scientists, ~25 rubric criteria/task (~19,020 total); best model GPT-Rosalind passed ~36.1% overall, fell from 45.1% text-only to 28.1% on tasks requiring real artifacts (genomic/chemical-structure files, URLs); OpenAI-authored, scores are the vendor's. NOTE for today: 3+ days old and not re-run since June 21 — a fresh continuation needs a NEW state-change (an independent/external submission on LifeSciBench, a successor model narrowing the artifact gap, or a competing benchmark). Re-citing the same 36.1% / 45.1%-to-28.1% figures must be DROPPED under ADR-002 Rule 2.
